identificationModule.briefTitle: Corifollitropin Alfa Versus Recombinant Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) in Ovarian Stimulation of Women Undergoing in Vitro Fertilisation

leadSponsor.name: National and Kapodistrian University of Athens

descriptionModule.briefSummary: The use of corifollitropin alfa is superior in terms of pregnancy outcome parameters as compared to recombinant follicle stimulating hormone (FSH) during ovarian stimulation protocols in women undergoing in vitro fertilisation.

armGroups.label: recombinant follicle stimulating hormone (FSH)
armGroups.description: 150-300 IU of FSH for ovarian stimulation in women undergoing IVF

interventions.name: corifollitropin alfa
interventions.description: 100 microg for a group of women weighing \<or=60 kg and 150 microg for a group of women weighing \>60 kg

interventions.name: recombinant follicle stimulating hormone (FSH)
interventions.description: 150-300 IU of the drug daily from day 2 of the menstrual cycle until more than 2 follicles are \>18mm

primaryOutcomes.timeFrame: at egg recovery, through study completion, an average of 2 years

secondaryOutcomes.measure: Clinical pregnancy rate cancellation rate miscarriage rate ectopic pregnancy rate
secondaryOutcomes.description: The presence of fetal heart at transvaginal ultrasound at 6+2 gestational weeks
The presence of fetal heart at ultrasound after 12 gestational weeks

eligibilityModule.eligibilityCriteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Women aged 18-36 years old with a body weight of more than 60 kg up to 90 kg
* BMI of 18-32 kg/m2
* Menstrual cycle length of 23-35 days
* An indication for controlled ovarian stimulation for IVF or ICSI

Exclusion Criteria:

* history of an endocrine abnormality
* abnormal outcome of blood biochemistry or hematology
* abnormal cervical smear
* chronic disease
* uterine pathology that interfering with the COS treatment (e.g. fibroids ≥ 5 cm)
